summary: Strong T2 module: unauth stats + cachedump + lru_crawler metadump + bounded multi-GET actually retrieve cached values with sensitive-shape tagging (session/JWT/csrf/apikey), and the UDP amplification probe measures a real amp ratio. Weakest area: no attempt at binary/SASL protocol probing (would let it distinguish SASL-enforced vs 'listening but broken'), no session-hijack chain (a captured JWT sample isn't fed to any HTTP module).

findings.tier_evidence: stats + stats items + stats cachedump return real key names and per-slab counts - proof of read.
findings.promotion_notes: Values-read is already emitted as a separate T2 (memcached_values_readable), which is the natural next tier for this kind.

findings.title_pattern: memcached cached values readable without credential
findings.tier_evidence: Multi-get retrieves actual cached bytes with 256B preview; ranks by session/JWT/csrf/apikey key-shape tags so the sample is the interesting ones.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = feed captured JWT/session tokens into the loot pool and auto-replay against paired HTTP services (matching hostname/vhost). Also emit a session-hijack Credential per value hit.
findings.tester_next_step: printf 'get <sensitive-key>\r\n' | ncat <ip> <port> ; then curl -H 'Cookie: SESSIONID=<hijacked>' https://<paired-app>/ to prove the hijack.

findings.tier_evidence: udp_stats_probe sends one UDP frame and measures reply size + amp ratio - positive verify (>=2x) only when UDP is actually answering.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 = additionally send a large `get <large-key>' UDP query to measure the historic ~51,000x amp; but that requires knowing a big-value key. Keep at T1 - single-datagram evidence is enough for reporting.
findings.tester_next_step: printf '\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00stats\r\n' | ncat -u <ip> <port> - measure reply size vs request size.

findings.promotion_notes: CVE-2016-8704/8705/8706 are binary/SASL integer overflows - emit them as version-gated kinds with a safe SASL-binary-header parse verify.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: loot.session_tokens (JWT/session values captured -> HTTP module replay)
hostname_pool (from any cached key metadata that names hosts)
amp_registry (record confirmed reflection sources for the engagement)
